messages.subject: Snapshots and point transect DS
parts:
Dear all,

I've some experience in line transect DS, and DS using camera-traps following Howe et al 2019 (https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.12790); but I'm new in point-transect DS.

My concern:

I’m now working on a project to estimate the Iberian goat (mountain ungulate) population density. This species is usually monitored from points and applying total counts or point-transect DS. However, I think that considering the theoretical background of CTDS will be very useful for this species, but considering human observers instead of camera-traps. So, the question is, do you think that it is correct to define snapshots moments considering a point-transect DS based on human observers? (obviously, during the analysis, I'll consider overdispersion: https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.13082).

Considering the habitat selected by these animals, the human effort of traveling between sampling points is very high. So in my opinion, it could be cost-efficient if we can carry out more than one sampling during each visit by considering snapshot moments (let say, 30min apart to locate and identify objects around the point).

 THANK YOU VERY MUCH!

Best

Pablo

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] Snapshots and point transect DS
parts:
Pablo, yes, that is fine.  Of course you assume the animals don’t respond to you as you walk into the point.  The time separation between snapshot moments should be sufficient that animals have moved around – if after 30 mins, most animals are largely where they were before, you gain little information.  (For a camera, this isn’t an issue, but for human observers, time at the point costs money …)

 

Steve Buckland
